labels.reason: wrapCss interpolates the rule value into an href attribute when GEN_URL_RE matches, and that regex allows double quotes, so a crafted value breaks out of the attribute in the injected HTML.

$ldap_loginsmb comes from LDAP directory attributes and is echoed unescaped into a value attribute and the page body, unlike the escaped GETPOST branch, so a user-controlled directory attribute can inject HTML.
$_SERVER["PHP_SELF"] includes attacker-controlled PATH_INFO and is concatenated unescaped into an href attribute.
$urlsource is built from the unescaped $_SERVER["PHP_SELF"] and passed to showdocuments for use in generated links and forms, so path-info content is reflected.
$_SERVER["PHP_SELF"] is placed unescaped into the form action attribute, and its path-info portion is attacker-controlled.
$_SERVER['PHP_SELF'] is concatenated unescaped into an href, so crafted path-info reflects into the page.
req.url is appended to base and reflected unescaped into HTML (including an href) in the 404 response of the dev/preview server.
$group is interpolated unquoted into SQL in SetInGroup, and callers such as the REST API setGroup and the SOAP webservice pass request-supplied values without an int cast.
The order is whitelisted by fixOrder, the limit is cast to int, and the content type list comes from field definitions in server configuration, not from end users.
table_name comes from the request path in this sample provider but only after exists()/get_resource_inst has matched it against the SHOW TABLES list, so arbitrary SQL cannot reach DESCRIBE.
islandContent, which embeds rendered slot content, is written raw inside an inline script element, and a literal </script> in slot HTML can break out; the shown code does not escape it.

Schema names are internal restore parameters from the adapter configuration and backup metadata, and the module defines assertPostgresSchemaIdentifier and quoting helpers for validating them, so no unvalidated request input is evident.
The checkpoint name is used unsanitized in a path join and file write, so a name like ../../x writes a .json file outside the checkpoints directory.
The SSID is passed through util.sanitizeString, which strips shell metacharacters, before it is placed in the netsh command.
The only caller passes a numeric statut comparison built from an integer search parameter, and the other call passes no filter, so no attacker-controlled SQL reaches $filter.
The session name is joined into a path and unlinked without sanitization, so a name containing ../ deletes arbitrary .json files; it comes from the user's session-delete command.
The output is a project link generated by getNomUrl from database-stored project fields entered by privileged internal users, and the tooltip content is escaped; no direct request data reaches it.
wrapJs interpolates the rule value into the src attribute with only a URL-shaped regex check that permits double quotes, so a crafted value breaks out of the attribute.
The module is tagged path_restricted, so path restriction is enforced by the framework's module guard; the shown code only creates directories for a caller-authorized output path.
The order is whitelisted by fixOrder, the amount is an int, and the slug comes from content-type configuration, not from user input.
$group and $entity come from callers that pass integer request values or database-fetched ids, so no attacker-controlled string reaches the DELETE query.
The user-supplied order value is only compared against the column list or HTML-escaped by select_input/optionlist, and the index $i is an integer, so it is not echoed unescaped.
$ldap_lastname from LDAP attributes is printed unescaped into a value attribute and the page, so a user-controlled directory attribute can inject HTML.
rid and module are escaped and quoted, and $entity comes from an integer-typed request value or from configuration, so the query is not injectable from the callers shown.
$ldap_mail from LDAP is printed unescaped into a value attribute, so a user-controlled directory attribute can break out and inject HTML.
$column is HTML built by select_input, which escapes option labels and values via optionlist/h(), with $i as an integer index and a constant onchange handler.
The history limit is a tool option interpolated into a shell command run through exec, with only a TypeScript type that is not enforced at runtime on JSON tool input.
$ldap_mobile from LDAP is printed unescaped into the page, so a user-controlled directory attribute can inject HTML.
$ldap_mail from LDAP is printed unescaped into the page body, so a user-controlled directory attribute can inject HTML.
$_SERVER['PHP_SELF'] is concatenated unescaped into an href attribute, and its path-info portion is attacker-controlled.
getGitHash is only called with the constant 'HEAD' in the code shown, so ref is not attacker-controlled.
rid is escaped and the module and perms values are escaped and quoted or come from the rights_def table, and callers pass integer-cast request values.
The href goes through cmNormalizeURL, which decodes, percent-encodes and ampersand-escapes the URL, and the title is entity-escaped, so no quote breakout is possible.
item.url from the imported Revue JSON is interpolated unescaped into an href attribute of the generated post HTML, so a crafted import file can inject markup.
$_SERVER['PHP_SELF'] is concatenated unescaped into an href attribute, and its path-info portion is attacker-controlled.
This only executes SQL generated by the builder's batch render methods, whose values and identifiers are escaped or protected upstream, and no unescaped request data is visible here.
The alt text is produced by stripping tags with a regex that mishandles attribute values containing '>', so a quote can survive into the alt attribute and break out of it.
The sessionId query parameter is placed unsanitized into a path.join filename, so ../ sequences inside it can traverse out of the data directory to read other .jsonl files.
$_SERVER["PHP_SELF"] is passed unescaped into the confirmation form URL, and its path-info portion is attacker-controlled.
